## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to design a dynamic 2D data structure with non-trivial aggregates, not just sums.

## Key Concepts
- 2D range trees with implicit keys
- per-node color-frequency maps for mode queries
- coordinate compression to bound memory
- correct handling of duplicates via counts

## Code Example
```javascript
// Skeleton: insert/erase and count/mode queries using per-node color maps
class Node {
  constructor() {
    this.x = 0; this.left = null; this.right = null;
    this.yTree = new BST(); // stores (y, color, delta)
    this.colorCounts = new Map(); // color -> count
  }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you bound memory in degenerate inputs?
- How would you adapt to online vs offline coordinate distributions?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical use of order-statistics-like queries with dynamic inserts/deletes in a real-world analytics context.

## Key Concepts
- Coordinate compression
- Fenwick tree (BIT) for prefix sums
- Handling duplicates and unseen thresholds

## Code Example
```javascript
class BIT {
  constructor(n){ this.n=n; this.t=Array(n+1).fill(0);} 
  add(i, delta){ for(; i<=this.n; i+=i&-i) this.t[i]+=delta; }
  sum(i){ let s=0; for(; i>0; i-=i&-i) s+=this.t[i]; return s; }
}
```

- How would you handle dynamic value domains without a pre-pass?
- What are trade-offs vs a balanced BST-based order-statistics tree?
